images.alt: DSA Statement. We Stand in Solidarity with Chicago Alderman Byron Sigcho-Lopez. 6/15/26. DSA stands united against attacks on our members. We are appalled by the rising tide of political violence in this country which culminated last night in an explosive device detonated at the home of Chicago Alderman Byron Sigcho-Lopez. While we are relieved to hear that Byron and his family are safe, we understand this attack as an attempt at intimidation. Byron’s independent campaign for Congress is a challenge to the political establishment. DSA’s work across the country challenges the status quo and inspires working class people everywhere to organize for a better world. Our opponents believe they can use acts of terror to frighten us into silence, but they are wrong. DSA will ensure our local chapters continue their valuable work with security practices in place to keep our members safe. No one should have to fear retaliation for speaking the simple truth: workers deserve more.

For over a century, oppressed and exploited people around the world have carried the banner of socialism in the struggle to free themselves from a system that sees them as nothing more than raw material for a profit-making machine.

Today, socialists in the U.S. are leading the fight to democratize our economy and our government, to stop the endless wars at home and abroad, and to ensure that the wealth of the nation belongs to those who create it.

Photo: Workers marching behind a hand-made banner reading “We won’t fight another rich man’s war!!”

The Senators and members of Congress who oppose those goals have no program of their own to offer other than more suffering to maintain the status quo. Unable to confront the failures of their dead-end politics they fall back on stoking fear of socialism, fueling yet another Red Scare at home, and another Cold War abroad.

Americans have seen where that ends: decades of paranoia, censorship, corruption, 
murder, and war. 

We won’t fall for it again.

Photos of representatives who voted for the resolution.

The fight for socialism is the fight for human dignity. It’s only natural that it would be condemned by those who profit from human misery and exploitation.

With over 89,000 members across the country and counting, the fight is only getting stronger.

images.alt: Democratic Socialists of America, National Political Committee Statement. Stopping SNAP benefits is an attack on poor people. November 3, 2025. Read the full statement in English and Spanish at the link in our profile.

The government shut-down will mean that poor people in the United States will no longer receive SNAP benefits beginning November 1, 2025. This is class war, and as socialists it is necessary to fight back. Although our government has endless funding to commit genocide abroad, it claims poverty when it comes to feeding our own children here at home. Approximately 62% of SNAP recipients are in families with children, meaning that we are quite literally starving children right now. Why? Because the class that is in power right now thinks that starving children, whether in Gaza or in the United States, is an acceptable thing to do, and further thinks that it can get away with it without a fight. 1/3

As socialists we understand this is a feature and not a bug in the current political system of the United States. The Republican Party actively wants to starve this population, using dehumanizing language to describe individuals receiving public assistance. Food stamp recipients are victims of capitalism, not “parasites.” At the same time, the Democratic Party only wants to draw attention to this horror to the extent that it might benefit them electorally. If the Democratic Party wanted to do something, then it would exercise the power that it actually has at the local level. All across the country, in states led by Democratic governors, however, the response has been absolutely anemic. Even though the Democrats can choose to spend state funds to feed the children frozen out of the SNAP program, they have so far chosen to dodge the issue instead. As socialists, we need to increase the pressure on the individual states to exercise the power that they have right now. 2/3

Across the country, we have the ability to agitate within individual states and cities to fill the gaps that are being created by an utterly horrific federal government, and to make sure that everyone responsible — whether through action or inaction — for literally starving children faces the consequences of their decisions, rather than passive acceptance. 

This is why we also strongly encourage chapters to utilize existing DSA mutual aid and tenant networks to check on neighbors and connect them with resources. We cannot sit on our hands, because solidarity means showing up and actively fighting tooth and nail.

In solidarity. 3/3
